title: AH-1Z Viper (pilot)

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The AH-1Z Viper is the newest Cobra of the US Marine Corps (from 2010): a four-bladed rotor, two T700 engines and a glass cockpit with screens in both seats, shared with the UH-1Y Venom. The gunner in front aims the targeting sight; both crew members have helmet displays. The switches of its modern grips are not described in public sources, so JoyPro keeps the basic Cobra controls of the AH-1W (force trim, radio, rocket button, gun trigger, power levers), and this guide builds on the AH-1W guide.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The screens, the standby instrument and the data entry keyboard.

panels.name: Instrument panel (glass cockpit)
panels.text: Two colour screens and a smaller display in each seat, with a standby instrument and the master warning lights.
panels.context: The AH-1Z shares this glass cockpit with the UH-1Y Venom; the gauges of the older Cobras became pages on the screens.

controls.name: Multifunction displays (2)
controls.text: Two large colour screens (multi-function screens with buttons around their edge). They show the flight instruments, the map, the weapons, the targeting sensor picture and the engines.
controls.context: Instead of dozens of round dials, the crew picks the page each screen shows; one screen can replace another that fails.

controls.name: Dual-function display
controls.text: A smaller screen that shows the engine and fuel data, or a backup page when a big screen fails.
controls.context: It keeps the most important engine numbers in view while the big screens show the mission.

controls.name: MFD bezel keys
controls.text: Buttons around the edge of each screen. Each one picks the word printed next to it on the screen, so the same button does different things on different pages.
controls.context: The crew uses them to change pages and options; the page layout is not described in the sources JoyPro uses.

controls.name: Standby flight display
controls.text: A small separate instrument that shows the attitude (nose up or down, leaning left or right), the speed and the height. It keeps working when the big screens fail.
controls.context: It is the backup that lets the pilot fly safely to a landing if the main displays go dark.

controls.name: Master warning / caution lights
controls.text: Two big lights: master warning means "danger now", master caution means "something needs your attention". The message on the display says what is wrong.
controls.context: Pressing the light usually acknowledges it, so it is ready to show the next problem.

panels.name: Data entry keyboard
panels.text: A keyboard with a small screen for typing navigation, radio and weapon data.
panels.context: It replaces the separate radio boxes of the older Cobras; radios and navigation are set through it. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

controls.name: Keyboard
controls.text: Letter and number keys, like a small computer keyboard, for typing navigation points, frequencies and codes.
controls.context: The crew types what is needed, checks it on the scratchpad and sends it to the system.

controls.name: Scratchpad display
controls.text: A small text display that shows what has been typed before it is sent (the scratchpad).
controls.context: A typing mistake can be seen and corrected here before it changes anything.

controls.name: Function keys
controls.text: Keys that call up the pages for the radios, the navigation and the weapons.
controls.context: They choose what the typed data is for. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

areas.name: Left console
areas.text: The power levers of the two T700 engines.
